Claire — thanks, this is a great prompt. Attaching our hosted rate card and a short worked example below. I kept the math explicit so you can paste into your finance model.

[attachment: Redwood_Hosted_RateCard_2026Q3.pdf (pdf)]
[attachment: SOW_Sentinel_Retail_v1.docx (docx draft)]

High-level notes:
- List pricing: see attached PDF (hosted API token-based and response-unit options).
- Discounting: standard first-year committed discounts start at 10% for <$50k/mo committed, 15% for $50-150k/mo, and 20%+ for multi-year enterprise commits — final structure depends on term and support SLA.
- Bill triggers to watch: function/tool calling generates additional output tokens (billed as output tokens); streaming does not change per-token billing but increases number of billing events under some telemetry plans; default caching may reduce billable tokens for repeated prefixes.

Worked examples (monthly, using your numbers):
Assumptions shared: 50,000 user messages; avg user input = 50 tokens; avg assistant output = 350 tokens; 15% sessions have a second turn (assume second-turn user 40 tokens / assistant 180 tokens).

A) Legacy Chat Completions (token billing):
- Primary turns = 50k * (50 in + 350 out) = 50k * 400 = 20,000,000 tokens
- Follow-ups (15% of sessions => 7,500 sessions): 7.5k * (40 in + 180 out) = 7.5k * 220 = 1,650,000 tokens
- Total tokens = 21,650,000 tokens
- If list price = $0.0006 per token (hypothetical for illustration), monthly bill = 21,650,000 * 0.0006 = $12,990

B) Responses endpoint (response-units + token component):
- Responses pricing counts a response unit per assistant output + a small token multiplier for input/context. For your workload we model as: 1 response-unit per assistant reply + token-priced input+output at a lower per-token rate because of response bundling.
- Response units = 50k + 7.5k = 57,500 units
- Token component (combined): 21,650,000 tokens but at lower token rate; assume tokens priced at $0.00045/token and response-unit charge $0.0008/unit (illustrative).
- Token cost = 21,650,000 * 0.00045 = $9,742.50
- Response-unit cost = 57,500 * 0.0008 = $46.00
- Monthly bill = ~ $9,788.50 (~25% lower vs legacy token-only in this example)

C) Chat product (streaming/chat-optimized pricing):
- Chat product often bundles amortized prefix costs differently and provides better long-session efficiency. With our chat-optimized SKU assume token price $0.00042/token and a small per-request overhead of $0.0005 per chat-turn.
- Token cost = 21,650,000 * 0.00042 = $9,093
- Per-turn overhead = 57,500 * 0.0005 = $28.75
- Monthly bill = ~$9,122 (a touch cheaper than Responses in this profile)

Key takeaways and caveats:  
- If you have many short messages, response-unit models give better predictability and often lower bills because they decouple output length from a single expensive model token rate.
- Long assistant outputs favor chat/streaming SKUs that have optimized kernels and lower per-token pricing.
- Function calling will increase output tokens (payloads for tools) and may add metadata tokens; we can provide an example if you send a typical function payload.
- Committed discounts and reserved capacity (Redwood Dedicated) change unit economics dramatically; I included conservative discount bands above.

If you want, I can run the exact numbers into the attached SOW template and return a redlined estimate with a recommended commit to hit 15% blended first-year discount based on your projected run rate. If you can confirm expected monthly run-rate range (low/central/high), I’ll put together 2 pricing tiers (conservative commit and an aggressive commit with 18–20% discount).

Best,
